P1.evidence: All four clean. 'Abdul, I read through your application, man, so I have a bit of a head start, but what I'd love to do on this call, I want to get a really clear understanding of where you're at, where you're trying to get to, what's kind of missing, what's getting in the way... And then at the end, we can kind of plan out some next steps. That all sound good? Yep.' Followed by the open question: 'Walk me through it then. What could we potentially help you with today? Give me a bit of an overview.' Worth noting the rep held the frame under pressure — the prospect immediately asked him to skip to a product overview, and he redirected back to discovery rather than complying.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch. Height, weight and age all asked directly. Work and sedentary load established. Health conditions asked and confirmed. P2d is the standout and the best execution of that check anywhere in these twelve files: 'Any other injuries or chronic pain or anything?' followed by the duration question the script actually asks for — 'has this been something going on, like the knees, the shoulder, how long has that been going on for, all that?' — which produced two years for the shoulder, two for the knees, and the chronic lower back history. P2e was pressed properly rather than accepted: 'how many days did you go last week to the gym?', 'What about the week before?', 'what percentage of the time would you actually hit two to three days?', 'in the last three months, how many times a week on average?' — which moved a claimed two to three sessions down to an actual one or two. P2g is equally good and is the technique to propagate: rather than accepting 'my diet is pretty clean', he asked 'What did you eat yesterday?', then breakfast and lunch specifically, then 'What's your guilty pleasure?', which surfaced eggs, potato, toast, a burger, rice and ice cream two days running. P2h partial — sleep apnea was captured as a condition and bedtime established, but sleep quality and quantity were not explored. P2i miss — energy was never asked.

P3.evidence: Also the strongest goals phase in the batch. P3a asked and then followed: 'how are we actually feeling about our body and our physique as a whole right now?' — 'not great' — 'why not, walk me through it.' P3d asked early and plainly. P3e is a proper future-pace with a genuine attempt to lift the prospect out of his own resignation first: 'you have to kind of stretch your mind with me a little bit and think outside of that, because otherwise, this isn't going to work... picture yourself... you've accomplished everything you want fitness wise... what would actually excite you? Not like what's realistic, but what would actually excite you?' P3f ran explicitly — 'where else does that show up in your life? Like, how else does that impact your life?' — and then the follow-up about relationship status surfaced a wife and five children. P3g reached identity, confidence, introversion, marriage, children and the breadwinner role. P3h is a real reflect-back with a check attached: 'Correct me if I'm wrong, man, but it sounds like there's maybe a little bit of apathy or resignation around the whole idea of losing weight,' answered 'I do feel that sometimes.' That is the best reflect-back in the batch because it named the emotional obstacle rather than the goal.

P4.evidence: A complete phase and the only one in the batch to score hit on every check. P4a: 'I want to dive a little bit more into why you feel like those other programs didn't work' and 'How many bootcamps and how many times have you worked with a trainer the last little bit?' P4b: 'what's missing? Like when we fall off or when we bounce back, like what happens, what changes?' P4c: 'Why do you feel you fall off track when you do, like what happens?' P4e: the prospect named the gap himself — the six-week bootcamp ends, nobody holds him accountable, he lets loose. P4f is the crucial one and it ran almost exactly as scripted, which no other call in this batch managed: 'there's never going to be anybody holding, you know, I mean, you can have somebody hold you accountable for a period of time, but eventually, something's going to come to an end and you're back by yourself. So where do you think the missing link is to be able to hold yourself accountable? Why haven't we been able to hold ourselves accountable afterwards?' That is the right question at the right moment to the right prospect.

P5.evidence: The best consequence frame in the batch and the only one where the rep pushed past the first vague answer. Permission was taken first — 'do I have your permission to be completely straight and direct with you, man, and not beat around the bush at all?' — which is good practice for what followed. P5a was asked with a strong set-up tied to his own disclosed health issues: 'if we don't get this handled and find something that's sustainable and actually create an identity change, what's going to happen over the next two, three, four, five years? What's life going to look like?' The prospect gave a vague answer, 'I think the health is going to deteriorate more', and instead of accepting it the rep pressed twice: 'Give me an example. What would that look like?' and then 'Why not for your family though? How's it going to impact your family?' That produced the breadwinner answer, and the follow-up — 'What kind of an example do you feel like your lifestyle and your health is setting for your...' — produced 'Yeah, probably not a good one, for sure.' P5b and P5c are partial because the specific scripted questions were not used, though functional equivalents ran. P5d is a miss: the line-in-the-sand question was never asked, which is a direct consequence of the call running out of time.

P6.evidence: Unreachable. The prospect called a hard stop at six o'clock after the training and nutrition pillars, before the accountability pillar and the delivery walkthrough, so the commitment check was never arrived at. Dropped from the denominator. The underlying issue is time management rather than technique — fifty-two minutes were spent and two of three pillars delivered, and the prospect had flagged nothing about his availability at the outset.

P11.evidence: No price was presented and no close attempted, so the phase does not apply. The equivalent action, securing the next call, was handled properly: a specific time was agreed for Wednesday at 4pm Central, the invite was duplicated and sent live, a confirmation text was arranged for the morning, and homework was set.

notes: The best-run process in this batch on every phase that was reached, and it should be used as the reference call for P2, P3 and P4. Three techniques to propagate verbatim: asking what the prospect actually ate yesterday meal by meal instead of accepting a self-assessment of the diet; narrowing claimed training frequency down to a real number across three questions; and running the self-accountability challenge in full on a prospect whose entire history is programmes that worked until the accountability stopped. Two corrections. First, time management — fifty-two minutes reached two of three pillars, the phase this prospect most needed to hear was the one that was never delivered, and the hard stop was discovered rather than established at the top. Second, and more seriously, the medical picture was gathered better here than anywhere else in the batch and then acted on nowhere: hypertension on medication, sleep apnea on CPAP, two years of knee problems ruling out running and jumping, a restricted shoulder and chronic lower back weakness were all captured with durations, and the only thing said about any of it afterwards was that the knee pain would start going away. That gap between excellent gathering and zero clinical action is the coaching point.
